messages:
anya: quick thread — we need to decide where format negotiation lives for weight sources (safetensors / sharded / zipped bundles). loader boundary or weightsource/transport?
marco: +1 for putting negotiation in weightsource/transport. keeps runtime loader simpler and avoids duplicating parsing logic across runtimes.
lee: strong +1. weightsource can return a canonical manifest that runtime consumes. less surface area.
sam: tradeoff: if weightsource hides fallback rules, runtime loses control. we need a strict contract: weightsource returns resolved manifest + checksums + semantics for hotstart.
oliver: proposal: tiny handshake proto so runtime can ask for "best" representation. e.g.
```
GET /weights?model=foo&ver=1&capabilities=hotstart,stream
200 OK
{
  "format": "safetensors+shardlist",
  "shards": ["s3://bucket/foo/s1","s3://bucket/foo/s2"],
  "checksums": ["sha256:aaa...","sha256:bbb..."],
  "hotstart_hint": [0,1],
  "compatibility_flags": ["lazy-hotstart"]
}
```
anya: we should include a `compatibility_flags` field to signal lazy vs eager warmup expectations and any runtime constraints. :thumbsup:
sam: also require deterministic shard ordering and an `eviction_tag` so warmup scheduler can reason about QoS/eviction groups.
marco: security note — runtime should enforce allowed checksum algorithms and key-signature verification. weightsource can't pick arbitrary algs.
lee: runtime validation idea: validate first N bytes + checksum before mmap to avoid silent corruption on cold starts.
oliver: fallback pattern: if weightsource cannot supply sharded safetensors, it should offer either a streaming adapter endpoint or an alternate compatible manifest (e.g., fused bundle). runtime can then decide fallback policy.
anya: and we need an error taxonomy: 4xx = manifest/compatibility (no retry, escalate), 5xx = transport (retry/backoff). warmup coordinator uses that to decide canary/rollback.
sam: also consider a request-time gating flag: `?gating=fast-warmup` so weightsource can trade off compact headers vs full provenance. good for cold-path faststarts.
marco: implementation plan: small shim in weight-proxy to translate legacy manifests -> new canonical manifest while we roll out. low-risk.
ci-bot: perf FYI — in the last canary, moving negotiation into runtime added ~3ms median model-load latency; offloading to weightsource was ~0.5ms. numbers look consistent across GPUs.
anya: action items: marco + lee draft handshake proto + error codes; oliver mock streaming adapter fallback; sam add gating tag to warmup scheduler; I'll file RFC follow-up and link to this thread.
lee: ack — will push draft by EOD.
marco: acked.
ci-bot: reminder: tag followup RFC PR with `eng-ml/warmup` so CI collects perf traces.
